summary: Telnet (RFC 854) is a cleartext remote-terminal protocol whose mere presence in 2026 is itself a finding — every keystroke, credential, and command is on the wire. Attackers care about it as a foothold with three properties: (1) it hands out an OS/vendor fingerprint through the pre-auth banner and login-prompt style (Cisco 'User Access Verification', Juniper 'login:', Linux 'Ubuntu 22.04 LTS\nlogin:', BusyBox '(none) login:', Solaris 'SunOS 5.10'); (2) it negotiates options via IAC that leak host state — NEW-ENVIRON (RFC 1572) can be tricked into revealing USER/DISPLAY/HOME/JOB/PRINTER/DOMAIN, TTYPE reveals the client's terminal expectation, and the presence/absence of ENCRYPT (RFC 2946) and AUTHENTICATION (RFC 2941) options tells you whether creds will fly cleartext; (3) legacy telnetd builds have unauthenticated RCEs and login-bypass bugs (Solaris CVE-2007-0882 in.telnetd -f arg injection, inetutils/netkit CVE-2020-10188 encrypt_keyid overflow, dozens of BusyBox/embedded devices with hardcoded creds). recce currently only harvests nmap's telnet-encryption/telnet-ntlm-info NSE output; a dedicated module can add a stdlib IAC negotiator, prompt-style fingerprinting, ENVIRON leak probe, and a small known-default-creds sweep, and it can enrich known_hostnames/known_users/relay_targets from what the banner and prompt reveal.

existing_coverage.notes: serviceenum.py maps nmap service name 'telnet' and TCP/23 to the 'telnet' script bucket (line 12, 38). core/scanner.py enables the nmap NSE scripts telnet-encryption and telnet-ntlm-info (line 254); parser.py turns a telnet-encryption 'does not support encryption' hit into a medium 'Telnet without encryption (cleartext)' finding with CWE-319 (parser.py:296). svcdetect.py does NOT list 23 in PORT_NAMES (relies on nmap for that well-known port) and there is no signature/nudge for telnet in _SIGNATURES/_NUDGE. There is NO recce/services/telnet.py — no stdlib IAC probe, no banner-fingerprint enrichment, no ENVIRON leak check, no default-cred sweep, no runbook, no findings mapper, no known-bad-build map. rservices.py (recce's closest peer for a 'presence-is-the-finding' legacy protocol) is the style template.

capabilities.name: iac_option_negotiation_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Read the pre-auth IAC DO/WILL/DONT/WONT negotiation stream and record the set of options the server offers/refuses — the pattern (WILL ECHO, WILL SUPPRESS-GA, DO TERMINAL-TYPE, DO NAWS, DO NEW-ENVIRON, DO/WILL ENCRYPT, DO/WILL AUTHENTICATION) is a strong OS/vendor fingerprint distinct from the banner and grounds every other finding.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 854 Sec 'The Telnet Command Structure' (IAC=255), RFC 855 (option negotiation)
capabilities.notes: Stdlib socket + a 4-byte IAC parser. Mirror the ftp.py style: a probe() that returns a dict {banner, options_will, options_do, encrypt_offered, auth_offered, environ_offered, prompt_style, vendor_guess}.

capabilities.name: cleartext_presence_is_the_finding
capabilities.description: Emit a HIGH baseline finding whenever telnet is open at all — the protocol offers no cleartext-protection option by default, so its presence on a 2026 network is a categorical control failure worth its own writeup (recce already does this pattern for rlogin/rsh in rservices.py).
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 854 (no encryption in the base protocol); RFC 2946 (Encryption option — optional, rarely negotiated)
capabilities.notes: This one is emitted with zero packets beyond the enum sweep — same shape as rservices._finding().

capabilities.name: encryption_option_absent
capabilities.description: Confirm the server never sends WILL ENCRYPT (option 38) during the IAC negotiation — meaning even a client that asked for it cannot get a private channel — and upgrade the presence finding with definite evidence rather than an assumption.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 2946 Sec 3 'Telnet Encryption Option', option code 38
capabilities.notes: Direct upgrade of the parser.py:296 nmap-NSE-derived finding — but recce should emit it itself so a scan without --script telnet-encryption still gets it. Also record whether AUTHENTICATION (option 37, RFC 2941) is offered — an unencrypted-but-authenticated login is still a Kerberos password oracle.

capabilities.name: environ_option_leak
capabilities.description: When the server sends DO NEW-ENVIRON (option 39), reply with IAC SB NEW-ENVIRON SEND VAR IAC SE requesting standard variables (USER, DISPLAY, JOB, ACCT, PRINTER, SYSTEMTYPE) and record every value the server volunteers — real telnetds have leaked USER and HOME pre-auth this way.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 1572 Sec 2 'Command Names and Codes' (SEND=1, VAR=0, VALUE=1, USERVAR=3); RFC 1408 (older ENVIRON option 36 with reversed VAR/VALUE)
capabilities.notes: Support BOTH option 36 (old ENVIRON, RFC 1408) and option 39 (NEW-ENVIRON, RFC 1572) — the semantic codes are reversed between them; a naive parser reads USER as VALUE and vice-versa. Leaked USER feeds known_users.

capabilities.name: banner_and_prompt_vendor_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Capture the pre-login banner text and the login prompt style and classify vendor/OS from a small regex table: 'User Access Verification' -> Cisco IOS, 'Username:'+'Password:' with no 'login:' -> Cisco/Juniper, '(none) login:' -> BusyBox/embedded, 'SunOS 5.\d+' -> Solaris, 'HP-UX' -> HP-UX, 'iLO' -> HP iLO BMC, 'ONTAP' -> NetApp — each vendor guess opens a different runbook.
capabilities.protocol_reference: No RFC — de-facto login(1)/getty(8) conventions; Cisco IOS 'User Access Verification' banner; RFC 854 IAC-stripping required before regex.
capabilities.notes: Must IAC-strip the byte stream before regex — the banner is interleaved with 3-byte IAC sequences. Vendor guess -> product/version for CVE map (feeds recce's offline CVE DB the same way ftp.py does).

capabilities.name: known_bad_build_map
capabilities.description: Match the banner/vendor against a small curated map of telnetd builds with pre-auth RCE or login-bypass CVEs — Solaris in.telnetd (CVE-2007-0882, USER=-froot bypass), inetutils/netkit telnetd (CVE-2020-10188, encrypt_keyid heap overflow), BusyBox telnetd embedded-device hardcoded creds, D-Link/TP-Link/Netgear telnet backdoors — each match becomes a critical pre-auth compromise finding with the referenced module.
capabilities.notes: Same shape as ftp.py _KNOWN_BAD table — deliberately narrow, only well-known high-confidence signatures.

capabilities.name: solaris_telnetd_dash_f_bypass
capabilities.description: When the fingerprint says Solaris 10 (banner 'SunOS 5.10') and the login prompt is reached, connect with the client-side argument USER=-fbin (or -froot) to trigger CVE-2007-0882 in.telnetd, which passes the tainted username as a login(1) -f flag and grants an unauthenticated shell as that user.
capabilities.notes: Gate this behind explicit RECCE_ACTIVE_ATTACKS=1 like sqli.py does — it produces a live shell on a real host. Runbook uses `telnet -l -fbin <ip>`.

capabilities.name: login_prompt_timing_user_enum
capabilities.description: Measure the wall-clock delay between a valid vs invalid username and record the differential — many telnetd builds (particularly wrapping PAM) leak username validity through the timing of the password prompt, giving a low-noise pre-auth user enumeration primitive that feeds known_users.
capabilities.protocol_reference: No RFC — implementation artifact of login(1)/PAM. Similar to SSH's classic timing enum.
capabilities.notes: Requires a baseline (feed 3 clearly invalid usernames, average, then test candidates). Cheap: 3 short TCP sessions. Only run when known_users has candidates to test.

capabilities.name: default_and_hardcoded_credential_sweep
capabilities.description: Try a small, vendor-conditioned default-cred list (cisco/cisco, admin/admin, admin/<blank>, root/root, root/<blank>, root/xc3511 [Dahua/Xiongmai IoT backdoor], support/support, ubnt/ubnt) — telnet on embedded devices routinely accepts them, and each hit is credentialed shell.
capabilities.protocol_reference: No RFC — vendor default-credential databases (Cirt.net, Mitre BOTNET reports for Mirai's telnet cred list)
capabilities.notes: Vendor-conditioned: only try Cisco defaults when the banner said Cisco, Xiongmai/Dahua defaults when banner matches, etc. — avoids lockouts on real hosts. Successful cred -> relay_targets (try same on SSH/HTTP/SNMP).

capabilities.name: credentialed_privilege_and_hostname_capture
capabilities.description: Where creds are supplied or discovered, log in and capture 'uname -a', 'hostname', 'id', 'show version' (Cisco), '/etc/passwd' head — the resulting hostname/domain/user list feeds known_hostnames, known_users, and known_domains; the OS/version feeds the CVE DB.
capabilities.notes: Reuses the vendor guess from banner_and_prompt_vendor_fingerprint to pick the right identity commands ('show version' on Cisco, 'uname -a' on *nix). Cisco 'show running-config' reveals SNMP RO/RW and enable secret hashes -> known_hashes (hashcat -m 500/9200).

capabilities.name: ntlm_auth_option_leak
capabilities.description: When the server offers Microsoft's telnet AUTHENTICATION sub-option NTLM and completes an NTLM Type-2 challenge, extract the AV_PAIR fields (NetBIOS/DNS computer name, domain, forest, timestamp) — same data class the nmap NSE telnet-ntlm-info already surfaces, but recce owns it and can wire the values into known_hostnames/known_domains directly.
capabilities.notes: Only triggers on Windows Telnet Server (rare in 2026 but still on old Windows Server boxes). Replaces the parser.py reliance on the nmap NSE.

capabilities.name: cleartext_capture_witness
capabilities.description: Cross-service note that any capture of a telnet session (tcpdump 'tcp port 23') yields USER, PASSWORD, and every keystroke in cleartext — recce should emit an explicit MITM/sniff runbook line and flag the target for the segmentation-review writeup, because the finding's real weight is 'anyone on-path already has these creds'.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 854 (no encryption); RFC 2946 (Encryption optional and normally not negotiated)
capabilities.notes: Runbook line: 'tcpdump -i <iface> -A -s0 tcp port 23'. Also cross-references to arpspoof/ettercap in an ROE-appropriate way.

capabilities.name: telnets_tls_wrapped_variant
capabilities.description: On 992/tcp (or any port where the initial bytes look like a TLS ClientHello response), complete a TLS handshake first and negotiate IAC options over the TLS session — telnets is rare but exists on Cisco/legacy printers, and recce currently ignores it.
capabilities.notes: Reuse svcdetect.tls_http_probe() pattern for the TLS wrap, then hand off to the same IAC parser.

capabilities.name: iac_control_byte_smuggling_probe
capabilities.description: Send a benign IAC AYT (Are You There, IAC 246) and record whether the server responds — 'IAC AYT' presence proves the peer is speaking telnet and not a rogue app on 23, disambiguating misidentified ports (many bootloader/serial-console proxies squat on 23 with only a raw banner).
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 854 Sec 'Standard Representation of Control Functions' (AYT=246)
capabilities.notes: Cheap disambiguator, avoids emitting the whole finding tree on a port that looks like telnet but is actually a Cisco console concentrator or U-Boot serial.

recommended_findings.title: Telnet does not offer the ENCRYPT option (all traffic cleartext)
Telnet NEW-ENVIRON leaks environment variables pre-auth
Telnet daemon is a known-backdoored/RCE build
Telnet login-prompt timing enables username enumeration
Telnet NTLM AV_PAIR discloses NetBIOS/DNS/domain info

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: Cisco IOS $1$ (MD5-crypt) — 'enable secret 5' hash captured from a Cisco telnet session's 'show running-config'
Cisco IOS PBKDF2-SHA256 'enable secret 9' hash from 'show running-config'
Cisco Type 7 obfuscated password (reversible, not really a hash) from 'password 7 ...'
descrypt / traditional Unix crypt(3) hash from /etc/passwd or /etc/shadow on ancient AIX/HP-UX/Solaris via telnet shell
NetNTLMv2 challenge-response captured from a Windows Telnet Server AUTHENTICATION-option NTLM exchange

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames <- server hostname parsed from the pre-login banner ('hostname login:'), from Cisco 'User Access Verification\n<hostname>>' prompt, and from NTLM AV_PAIR MsvAvNbComputerName/MsvAvDnsComputerName when the AUTHENTICATION option is used
known_hostnames <- fully-qualified DNS name from NTLM AV_PAIR MsvAvDnsComputerName/MsvAvDnsTreeName
known_domains <- NTLM AV_PAIR MsvAvNbDomainName/MsvAvDnsDomainName/MsvAvDnsTreeName from telnet AUTHENTICATION option 37
known_users <- USER/LOGNAME leaked pre-auth via NEW-ENVIRON (RFC 1572) SEND response
known_users <- usernames confirmed by login-prompt timing enumeration
known_users <- account names harvested from /etc/passwd or Cisco 'show running-config username' after a credentialed shell
known_hashes <- Cisco 'enable secret 5/9' and 'username X secret' hashes from a credentialed 'show running-config' (hashcat -m 500/9200)
known_hashes <- descrypt hashes from /etc/shadow on an ancient Solaris/AIX/HP-UX shell (hashcat -m 1500)
known_hashes <- captured NetNTLMv2 blob from Windows Telnet Server AUTHENTICATION exchange (hashcat -m 5600)
relay_targets <- any credential that worked on telnet gets fanned out to SSH/HTTP-admin/SNMP/FTP on the same host and to the rest of the subnet (embedded devices share creds ruthlessly)

NEW shared surface: known_vendors — 'cisco-ios', 'juniper', 'busybox', 'solaris', 'hp-ilo', 'netapp-ontap' from banner/prompt fingerprint; gate subsequent modules' cred lists and NSE choices on this rather than re-guessing per module

NEW shared surface: cleartext_credentials_observed — a flag on the host/segment recording that a cleartext-auth protocol is exposed, so the segmentation/MITM writeup can aggregate telnet/ftp/http-basic/pop3/imap into one blast-radius argument
implementation_notes: Model this on recce/services/ftp.py: a probe(ip, port, timeout) that returns a dict, ftp_targets()-style discovery, a _KNOWN_BAD regex table, a finding_builder-based findings(), credfree_runbook()/cred_runbook(), and analyze(). But the byte layer differs: telnet is a duplex IAC-negotiated stream, not a line-mode ASCII protocol, so a small IAC parser is required — read into a buffer, split on IAC (0xFF), interpret 3-byte IAC WILL/WONT/DO/DONT (options 0x00..0xFF), handle IAC IAC as literal 0xFF, and buffer sub-negotiation between IAC SB and IAC SE. The initial 'passive-listen for the first 2s of IAC negotiation, then respond' pattern is enough for the fingerprint + ENVIRON leak capabilities without ever hitting a login prompt. Reuse recce/core/proxy.scaled() for timeout scaling under a pivot, same as svcdetect.grab_banner(). Add 23 to svcdetect PORT_NAMES and add a telnet signature to _SIGNATURES (a heuristic: any early sequence containing 0xFF 0xFB or 0xFF 0xFD is IAC and 90% telnet) so an unlabelled port on 2323/5555 gets picked up. Add a nudge b'\xff\xf6' (IAC AYT) to _NUDGE for port 23 so silent telnetds still surface. Reuse svcprobe.iter_probe() and svccommon.finding_builder / findings_to_vulns exactly like ftp.py does — no new plumbing. Gate the exploit capability (solaris_telnetd_dash_f_bypass) and the default-cred sweep behind RECCE_ACTIVE_ATTACKS=1 following the sqli.py pattern. Add a telnet script bucket under recce/scripts/services/ so recce-service.sh has something to invoke (serviceenum already routes 23 to 'telnet' but the script file does not exist yet).
